outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the problem has moved: unrefereed preprints posted 3 August to 10 October 2026 report bounded non-ball domains that lack the Pompeiu property, including a noncircular simply connected planar domain (Colbrook and Stepaniants), infinitely many N-fold symmetric planar domains (Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont), and convex non-ball domains in several dimensions (Guo, with claimed coverage of dimensions 2 to 18, 20 and 21 in v2); earlier in-window items are partial or analogue results, and the older claimed full solutions (Liu 2007, withdrawn; Ramm 2013 and 2016) have no uptake I could find.
problem_asks: Reading of the frozen statement (written before weighing any event). For a bounded domain D in Euclidean space R^n, call D a Pompeiu domain if the only continuous (or locally integrable) function f whose integral over every congruent copy (rigid-motion image) of D is zero is f = 0. The statement asks, in the Pompeiu problem's topological form: (A) for n = 2, which bounded domains with a given topology are Pompeiu domains; (B) the conjectured answer for that topological class, namely that a domain in the class fails the Pompeiu property only if it is a ball (equivalently, every non-ball domain in the class is a Pompeiu domain); (C) the same question in every dimension n ≥ 3, which is a separate part from n = 2. The statement does not fix which topology is meant. The Wikipedia lead wording reproduced in the sources is 'simply connected Lipschitz domain'; Ramm's wording uses 'connected complement' (for bounded planar domains these coincide). Background not asked: balls fail the property (Chakalov 1944); Williams (1976) equates failure with an overdetermined Neumann eigenfunction for smooth contractible / sphere-boundary domains.

events.what_happened: A. G. Ramm, ‘On symmetry problems’, arXiv:math/0504035. The abstract, as fetched, reads ‘withdrawn Several symmetry problems are discussed. These include the Pompeiu problem and similar conjectures for the heat and wave equations.’ No result on the Pompeiu problem is stated in the abstract.
events.revisions: v1 2 Apr 2005; v2 18 Apr 2005; v3 20 Apr 2005 (marked withdrawn).
events.delivers: Nothing specific; discusses the Pompeiu problem as one symmetry problem. Establishes no case.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: Withdrawn preprint; no content to assess.
events.direction: No claim made.

events.what_happened: Fabrício Caluza Machado and Sinai Robins, ‘The null set of a polytope, and the Pompeiu property for polytopes’, arXiv:2104.01957 (math.MG). Shows the null set of the Fourier–Laplace transform of a polytope in R^d does not contain almost all circles, hence no polytope fails the Pompeiu property; the abstract calls this an explicit proof that all polytopes have the property. The page notes Brown, Schreiber and Taylor (1973) for d = 2 and Williams (1976) for d ≥ 2.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv. A journal version is reported in a FAPESP record (Journal d’Analyse Mathématique, 2023) that I did not verify.
events.delivers: Pompeiu property for every polytope in R^d (a complete result for the polytope class, by the abstract’s account).
events.remains: All non-polytopal bounded domains, including smooth and simply connected ones; the balls-only question.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: polytopes are not balls and have the property.

events.what_happened: Genqian Liu, ‘Solution of the Pompeiu problem (I)’, arXiv:0711.3383 (math.AP). Earlier versions claimed (per the search summary, which I did not verify against those versions) that among bounded planar open sets with connected Lipschitz boundary only disks fail the Pompeiu property. The final v6 abstract reads only ‘This paper has been withdrawn by the author due to some errors.’
events.delivers: As claimed in earlier versions: the planar case (n = 2) of the conjecture. Withdrawn; establishes nothing on the record as it stands.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the author for ‘some errors’; the errors are not identified in the sources I read. I found no published refutation and no acceptance.

withdrawn.what: v6 abstract: ‘This paper has been withdrawn by the author due to some errors.’

events.direction: Claims the planar conjecture in the conjectured direction (only balls fail). Would contradict the 2026 planar counterexamples if it stood.

events.what_happened: Genqian Liu, ‘Solution of the Pompeiu problem (II)’, arXiv:0712.2753. The v1 claim, as reported in a search summary I did not verify against v1, is a proof of the Schiffer conjecture for n ≥ 3, hence of the Pompeiu problem in every n ≥ 2, building on part (I). The v2 abstract reads ‘This paper has been withdrawn by the author.’
events.delivers: As reported for v1: all dimensions n ≥ 3 via the Schiffer route. Withdrawn; establishes nothing on the record.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.doubts: Withdrawn; the v1 content was not opened by me. No public refutation or acceptance found.

withdrawn.what: v2 abstract: ‘This paper has been withdrawn by the author.’

events.direction: As reported: claims the conjectured direction in all dimensions n ≥ 3.

events.what_happened: A. G. Ramm, ‘A solution to the Pompeiu problem’, arXiv:1304.2297 (math.AP). Theorem 1 (as stated in the abstract): for n = 2, D bounded with closure diffeomorphic to a closed ball, smooth boundary and connected complement, and f in L¹_loc not identically zero with zero integrals over every rigid motion of D, then D is a ball. A corollary covers a Helmholtz problem. No journal reference or withdrawal notice on the arXiv page; the proof is not in the abstract.
events.delivers: Claimed: the planar case, restricted to domains whose closure is diffeomorphic to a closed ball (a topological hypothesis) with smooth boundary. The abstract states n = 2; a search summary says the argument generalises to n > 2, which I did not verify.
events.remains: Domains not diffeomorphic to a ball; n ≥ 3 as far as the abstract shows.
events.doubts: No publication or independent check found. Direct tension: the 2026 Colbrook–Stepaniants domain is bounded, has real-analytic boundary and is a conformal image of the disc, so its closure is diffeomorphic to a closed disc and it fails the Pompeiu property, which Theorem 1 says cannot happen unless it is a ball. One of the two must be wrong; I have not resolved which. The abstract is garbled in its connectivity sentence.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured direction (only balls fail) for the planar case under a ball-diffeomorphism hypothesis. Cuts against the 2026 planar counterexamples if correct.

events.what_happened: A. G. Ramm, ‘Solution to the Pompeiu problem and the related symmetry problem’, arXiv:1606.05976 (math.AP). Theorem 1 (as quoted by the fetch of the abstract): in R³, for a bounded domain D with C¹ boundary, ‘If D has P-property, then D is a ball.’ Theorem 2 (Helmholtz with u|S = 1, u_N|S = 0) gives a ball. The fetch reports the group for R³ as SO(2), which I could not confirm. No journal reference.
events.delivers: Claimed: the three-dimensional case for C¹ bounded domains, which the title and Theorem 1 present as a resolution in R³.
events.remains: n = 2 beyond Ramm 2013 (if that stands); n ≥ 4.
events.doubts: Theorem 1 as quoted says ‘if D has P-property then D is a ball’, the reverse of the conjecture as stated elsewhere in the sources (balls are the non-Pompeiu domains); this may be a transcription or convention issue and needs the full text. The SO(2) versus SO(3) point is unchecked. Tension with 2026 3D convex counterexamples (Guo, arXiv 2609.35419 v1), which if correct are non-ball domains failing the property.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured direction in R³. Cuts against the 2026 3D convex counterexamples if correct.

events.what_happened: Guowei Dai and Yong Zhang, ‘Sign-changing solutions to Schiffer’s overdetermined problem on wavy cylinder’, arXiv:2307.11797 (math.AP). Claimed unbounded wavy-cylinder domains in R^(N+1) with a bounded sign-changing Neumann-type solution, presented as counterexamples to Schiffer’s conjecture for unbounded domains and as non-spherical unbounded regions without the Pompeiu property. All versions withdrawn.
events.revisions: v1 21 Jul 2023; v2 25 Jul; v3 31 Jul; v4 11 Aug; v5 8 Sep 2023; v6 13 Oct 2023 (withdrawn).
events.delivers: As claimed: counterexamples for unbounded domains only. Withdrawn; bears on the bounded problem only by analogy.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks for bounded domains.
events.doubts: Authors state: ‘We find that the proof of our main Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.2 are wrong.’

withdrawn.what: All versions withdrawn: ‘We find that the proof of our main Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.2 are wrong.’

events.direction: Claimed counterexamples to Schiffer for unbounded domains; analogue, not the bounded problem.

events.what_happened: Luigi Provenzano and Alessandro Savo, ‘Isoparametric foliations and the Pompeiu problem’, arXiv:2108.13706 (math.DG). Gives spectral conditions under which level domains of isoparametric functions on compact Riemannian manifolds fail the Pompeiu property, with calculations for the round sphere.
events.delivers: Results on compact Riemannian manifolds with isoparametric foliations, including the round sphere. The abstract does not present a Euclidean result.
events.remains: The Euclidean problem for R^n.
events.direction: Analogue on manifolds; no direct bearing on Euclidean domains as the abstract presents it.

events.what_happened: Gergely Kiss and Miklós Laczkovich, ‘Solutions to the discrete Pompeiu problem and to the finite Steinhaus tiling problem’, arXiv:2403.01279 (math.FA). For a finite set K in R^k (k ≥ 2), a function summing to zero over every congruent copy of K vanishes identically; a stronger weighted version is proved; every finite set with at least two points is a Jackson set.
events.delivers: Discrete analogue: sums over finite point sets, not integrals over domains. Establishes the discrete property for every finite set in R^k, k ≥ 2.
events.remains: The classical problem: integrals over bounded domains of continuous or locally integrable functions. Nothing there is established.
events.direction: Positive, but for a different question (finite sums). Does not move the classical problem.

events.what_happened: Mihail N. Kolountzakis and Emmanuil Spyridakis, ‘Curves in the Fourier zeros of polytopal regions and the Pompeiu problem’, arXiv:2404.03405 (math.CA, cross-list math.AP). Proves that any finite union of interior-disjoint polytopes in R^d has the Pompeiu property, in every dimension, with a simpler planar proof; per the paper, this result was first proved by Williams (1976). Also shows complex spheres of any centre and certain rational curves cannot lie in the zero set of the transform.
events.revisions: v1 4 Apr 2024; no later version found.
events.delivers: Pompeiu property for finite unions of interior-disjoint polytopes in R^d, all d. Polytopal regions only; a new proof of a case already known by its own account.
events.remains: All bounded non-polytopal domains, including every smooth or simply connected non-polygonal case.
events.doubts: The ‘first proved by Williams’ attribution is as read through a fetch summary; check the body. No review found.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: non-ball polytopal unions have the property. Positive on a class containing no balls or smooth domains.

events.what_happened: Diaraf Seck, ‘On Pompeiu’s-Schiffer’s Conjectures from Shape Optimization’, arXiv:2405.11700 (math.AP, v1 only). Uses shape optimization, maximum principles and Serrin’s symmetry method. Theorem 4.2 (read in the HTML): for a bounded convex planar Ω with k² a Dirichlet eigenvalue and constant c₀ > β(R), the overdetermined problem has a solution, and the paper then states ‘As consequence, in this case the Schiffer’s conjecture is true (Ω is a disc).’ The abstract says only ‘We propose a way to get affirmative answers in some cases.’ The paper states the Pompeiu conjecture remains open.
events.delivers: Claimed: for bounded convex planar domains satisfying the Theorem 4.2 hypotheses, the Schiffer-type overdetermined problem forces a disc. Restricted to n = 2, convexity, a Dirichlet-eigenvalue condition and a constant condition; the Pompeiu property is not claimed.
events.remains: The Pompeiu problem in general; non-convex domains; n ≥ 3.
events.doubts: The proof sketch (§4.2.2) reduces to a disc through shape optimisation and an approximation argument that the fetched text describes as brief and not fully justified. Not peer reviewed. Whether Guo’s planar strictly convex non-disc counterexample (v2, Oct 2026) meets these hypotheses is not established.
events.direction: In favour of the conjectured rigidity (disc) for a restricted convex planar class, under the stated hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Michael J. Puls, ‘The Pompeiu problem and spherical spectral analysis’, arXiv:2505.03048 (math.FA, v1 only). For a compact set E in G/K with (G, K) a Gelfand pair, gives necessary and sufficient conditions for the Pompeiu property via K-spectral analysis.
events.delivers: A characterisation of a Pompeiu-type property on homogeneous spaces G/K. Not Euclidean R^n with congruences; names no balls or spheres as a result.
events.remains: The Euclidean problem entirely.
events.direction: None on the Euclidean problem; analogue on homogeneous spaces.

events.what_happened: Gonzalo Cao-Labora and Antonio J. Fernández, ‘A contractible Schiffer counterexample on the half-sphere’, arXiv:2510.05732 (math.AP, cross-list math.DG). Constructs a family of smooth contractible domains in S² with a Neumann eigenfunction constant on the boundary, by local bifurcation around geodesic disks centred at the north pole, with computer-assisted checks of the bifurcation conditions.
events.delivers: Schiffer-type counterexamples on the sphere. Not Euclidean; the abstract does not address the Pompeiu property.
events.remains: The Euclidean Schiffer and Pompeiu problems.
events.doubts: The computer-assisted bifurcation checks are the authors’ own; no review found.
events.direction: Against Schiffer’s conjecture on the sphere. Analogue for the Pompeiu question.
events.object: Smooth contractible domains on the half-sphere admitting a nontrivial Neumann eigenfunction constant on the boundary; existence by bifurcation (non-constructive), with computer-assisted verification of the bifurcation conditions.

events.what_happened: Guowei Dai, Yingxin Sun, Juncheng Wei and Yong Zhang, ‘On the Schiffer and Berenstein conjectures with high-frequency for convex domains in the plane’, arXiv:2511.19819 (math.AP). Dirichlet-type case: for a bounded uniformly convex planar domain with C^(2,ε) connected boundary, a large-eigenvalue solution with u = 0 and constant nonzero normal derivative forces a disk. Neumann-type case (Theorem 1.2): for a bounded uniformly convex planar domain with connected Lipschitz boundary, an eigenfunction at eigenvalue α > α₀(Ω) with zero normal derivative and constant boundary value forces a disk; α₀(Ω) is an unspecified positive constant. The Pompeiu problem appears only as background.
events.delivers: Partial Schiffer and Berenstein rigidity in the plane, restricted to uniformly convex domains and eigenvalues above an unquantified threshold. Does not use or prove the Pompeiu property.
events.remains: Non-convex domains; eigenvalues at or below α₀(Ω); the Pompeiu property directly.
events.doubts: The threshold α₀(Ω) is unquantified as read, so I cannot tell whether Guo’s planar strictly convex example (eigenvalue k = 1, so α = 1, Oct 2026) lies above it. That is the point where this paper and Guo’s would conflict; it is not established either way. Full text not read beyond the theorem region.
events.direction: In favour of rigidity (disc) on the restricted convex, large-eigenvalue class.

events.what_happened: Matthew J. Colbrook and George Stepaniants, ‘A computer-assisted counterexample to the planar Pompeiu and Schiffer conjectures’, arXiv:2608.01579 (math.AP, cross-list math-ph and math.SP), v1 only. Theorem 1.1: a bounded, simply connected, noncircular domain Ω in R² with real-analytic Jordan boundary, invariant under the dihedral group D₁₀ of order 20, and a nonconstant real u with (Δ + k²)u = 0 in Ω, u = 1 and ∂νu = 0 on ∂Ω, for k in (31.967007261, 31.967007293). Lemma 1.2 (the Fourier transform of the indicator vanishes on the circle of radius k) gives failure of the Pompeiu property. Stated as a counterexample to Schiffer’s conjecture and to the planar Pompeiu conjecture for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains. A Shortcake talk by Stepaniants was given at Princeton on 16 Sep 2026; this is a talk, not a review.
events.delivers: Establishes (if correct) that one bounded simply connected noncircular real-analytic planar domain lacks the Pompeiu property. Planar and simply connected only: nothing for n ≥ 3, and no statement on other topologies. A single failing non-ball is enough to refute the planar form of the conjecture as worded.
events.remains: Every dimension n ≥ 3; the full description of which planar domains fail the property; the converse structure for other topologies.

machine_checked.system: Validated numerical certificate (radii-polynomial / Newton–Kantorovich contraction; MPFR interval arithmetic at ‘256256 bits’ as printed; not Lean)

events.directly_checkable: The domain is a conformal image φ(𝔻) with φ a ten-fold symmetric map close to an explicitly listed degree-301 polynomial. Certified constants as read: Y ≤ 1.59×10⁻¹⁰, Z ≤ 0.621, C₂ ≤ 122, C₃ ≤ 0.012, unique zero in a ball of radius 10⁻⁶. Hand-checking is infeasible; the deposit carries the checker. I did not re-run it.
events.doubts: No independent reproduction, expert review or journal acceptance found. The argument depends on the authors’ interval code. The fetched text includes an ‘AI declaration’ (see ai) about debugging. Dai et al. (2025) do not contradict this domain as far as the record shows, since its convexity is not stated.
events.direction: Against the conjecture as worded for n = 2 simply connected domains: asserts a non-ball member of the class lacks the Pompeiu property, where the conjecture says only balls do.
events.object: Ω = φ(𝔻): a bounded simply connected noncircular planar domain with real-analytic Jordan boundary, D₁₀-symmetric, close to an explicit degree-301 polynomial image of the disc. A nonconstant real eigenfunction u with ∂νu = 0 and u = 1 on the boundary exists for k near 31.967 (Schiffer counterexample). By Green’s identity the indicator’s Fourier transform vanishes on the circle of radius k, so Ω lacks the Pompeiu property. Existence is non-constructive, certified by a computer-assisted contraction around a numerical centre.

events.what_happened: Gonzalo Cao-Labora and Jaume de Dios Pont, ‘Counterexamples to Schiffer’s Conjecture’, arXiv:2608.05114 (math.AP, cross-list math.SP, MSC 35N25), v1 only. Disproves Schiffer’s and the planar Pompeiu conjectures by constructing infinitely many non-ball planar domains, N-fold symmetric for large N, via bifurcation in a relaxed problem with real N whose branch size is independent of N. The paper says a Lean certification of the main result and of Corollary 1.2 is on GitHub (jaumededios/Schiffer). The paper also says its own examples ‘do not require computer assistance’, in contrast to Colbrook and Stepaniants.
events.delivers: Infinitely many non-ball bounded planar domains satisfying the Schiffer and Pompeiu conditions, so failing the Pompeiu property (per the abstract). Restricted to n = 2 and to N-fold symmetric members for large N. Whether these domains are simply connected is not verified: a secondary summary says so, but I could not read that in the text.
events.remains: Dimensions n ≥ 3; whether the family covers other topologies; the full description of Pompeiu-failing planar domains.

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 (formalisation of the main result and Corollary 1.2, by the authors themselves)

events.directly_checkable: The bifurcation argument is in the paper; the Lean formalisation is in the repository (the README calls it ‘a sligthy different path’ from the paper because Mathlib lacks elliptic regularity). I did not check it for sorry.
events.doubts: The Lean formalisation is by the same authors, so it is not independent. Wikipedia and a tracker say the Lean proof was developed with AI models, but the authors’ own text I could read does not say so (see ai). The readable part of the arXiv HTML covered about 100k of 179k characters; the remainder was not read.
events.direction: Against the conjecture as worded for n = 2: non-ball planar domains lacking the Pompeiu property, infinitely many of them.
events.object: Infinitely many distinct non-ball planar domains, one for each large integer N, N-fold symmetric, obtained by bifurcation (non-constructive existence; the branch size is independent of N and branches from near integer N reach integer N). Explicit approximations are not given in the readable text.

events.what_happened: Matthew J. Colbrook, Siavash Sadeghi and George Stepaniants, ‘A computer-assisted counterexample to the planar Berenstein conjecture’, arXiv:2608.08953 (v1). A bounded simply connected non-disc planar domain with real-analytic boundary and D₁₃ symmetry, with k near 27.438 and a sign-changing eigenfunction (zero Dirichlet, constant nonzero Neumann data), disproving the unrestricted planar Berenstein conjecture. The paper states that Colbrook and Stepaniants produced the first counterexamples to the planar Pompeiu and Schiffer conjectures.
events.delivers: A counterexample to Berenstein’s conjecture (a different overdetermined problem). Not a Pompeiu result.
events.remains: The Pompeiu problem entirely; recorded as a neighbouring problem, not a resolution of this bullet.

The record notes a newer version exists.

events.what_happened: Jizhou Guo, ‘Convex counterexamples to the Schiffer and Pompeiu conjectures in dimensions three, four, six, eight, ten and fourteen’, arXiv:2609.35419 v1 (math.AP, 87 pages per listing), with the same material on Zenodo 23020893 (v3.0, 28 Sep 2026). Corollary 1.3: for n in {3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 14}, the bounded convex domains from Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 (real-analytic boundary diffeomorphic to S^(n−1), Neumann eigenfunction with u = 1 and ∇u = 0 on the boundary) fail the Pompeiu property. The Zenodo record also describes a strictly star-shaped non-convex 3D example. The method reduces the cases to rank-two compact Lie algebras (u(2), so(4), su(3), so(5), g₂) via Harish-Chandra’s radial formula and Kostant’s theorem, with computer-assisted contractions and interval bounds in Arb.

events.what_happened: Jizhou Guo, arXiv:2609.35419 v2 (titled in its HTML ‘Convex counterexamples to the Schiffer and Pompeiu conjectures in dimensions two to eighteen’; the abstract page keeps the v1 title). Theorem 1.1 covers convex non-ball counterexamples in dimensions 2 to 18, 20 and 21 (the README adds dimension 19 as certified). For the plane, a bounded strictly convex non-disc domain with real-analytic boundary carries a nonconstant solution of Δu + u = 0 with u = 1 and ∂νu = 0 (Schiffer-type, k = 1); a Berenstein-type planar example with u = 0, ∂νu = 1 (sign-changing, k = 1) is also given. The author says this is the first convex planar counterexample. All existence proofs are described as computer-assisted; the HTML has a section ‘Computer-assisted verification’.
events.revisions: v1 28 Sep 2026; v2 6 Oct 2026 (per the arXiv listing as reported by search; not confirmed on the abstract page).
events.delivers: Per the author: convex non-ball counterexamples in dimensions 2–18, 20, 21 (computer-assisted), including a planar strictly convex non-disc example at k = 1. Restricted to convex domains. Whether the planar example’s failure of the Pompeiu property is proved in the text is in Section 33, which I did not read.
events.remains: Non-convex domains; dimensions beyond 21 (the second paper claims more, see its event); the Pompeiu property of the planar example if Section 33 does not prove it.

disputes.summary: The first planar counterexample: Colbrook and Stepaniants posted on 3 Aug 2026 and Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont on 5 Aug 2026. Wikipedia calls the second ‘independent’. By posting date the first is Colbrook and Stepaniants. Guo’s v2 also claims ‘the first convex planar counterexample’, which is a separate priority claim, not checked against the Cao-Labora domains’ convexity.

Ramm 2013 (planar, closure diffeomorphic to a ball, smooth boundary) and Liu 2007 (planar, withdrawn) assert that only balls fail the Pompeiu property. The 2026 Colbrook–Stepaniants domain appears to satisfy Ramm’s hypotheses. Both cannot stand; this is not resolved in the record.

Ramm 2016 (R³, C¹ boundary, ‘if D has P-property then D is a ball’) against Guo’s 3D convex counterexamples (arXiv 2609.35419 v1). The quoted direction of Ramm’s Theorem 1 looks reversed relative to the conjecture; needs the full text.

Seck (2024, planar convex, claims the disc follows under Theorem 4.2) and Dai et al. (2025, uniformly convex planar, large eigenvalue forces a disc, threshold unquantified) against Guo’s planar strictly convex non-disc counterexample at k = 1. Whether Guo’s domain satisfies their hypotheses is not established.

Wikipedia’s lead (as fetched) presents the problem as a conjecture, while its Counterexample section says 2026 preprints ‘disproved both conjectures’. The Breakthrough Tracker lists the planar results as provisional and not peer reviewed. The EoM entry (not opened) predates these results.

AI attribution for Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont: Wikipedia says ‘developed with assistance from GPT-5.6 and Claude models’ and the tracker says GPT 5.5/5.6 and Claude models were used for numerical checks, proof drafts and exposition, with GPT 5.6 writing the Lean 4 verification. The authors’ own text I could read does not say this. Recorded as unverified; no system placed in ai.systems.

summary: The Wikipedia lead gives the statement as the conjecture that a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with the Pompeiu property failing must be a ball. The sources I opened are: the arXiv abstract or HTML of every in-window and key pre-window preprint named below; the GitHub README of aster2024/schiffer-pompeiu-counterexamples and the repository jaumededios/Schiffer; Zenodo records 22999607, 23006742, 23020893 and 21765287; the Wikipedia article (read through a summarising fetch); the Breakthrough Tracker record; the Princeton talk page; and scilag.net. The 2026 events are the main finding. Colbrook and Stepaniants (arXiv 2608.01579, 3 Aug 2026) give one bounded simply connected noncircular real-analytic planar domain with a validated certificate, which fails the Pompeiu property via Lemma 1.2; this is a counterexample to the planar form of the conjecture as worded, and says nothing for n ≥ 3. Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont (arXiv 2608.05114, 5 Aug 2026) give infinitely many N-fold symmetric planar non-ball domains by bifurcation; their paper says its examples ‘do not require computer assistance’, and the paper has a Lean certification in the authors’ repository. Guo (arXiv 2609.35419 v1 28 Sep, v2 6 Oct 2026; Zenodo 27–28 Sep; repository README 8 and 10 Oct) gives convex non-ball counterexamples in dimensions 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 14 (v1) and 2–18, 20, 21 with a planar convex example (v2), all computer-assisted; the second paper and Berenstein results are known only from the README. None of these is peer reviewed, and none had an expert reading I could find. Colbrook et al.’s Berenstein paper (2608.08953) and Guo’s Berenstein results are neighbouring problems and are recorded as such, not as resolutions. In-window partial results are Kiss–Laczkovich (discrete, different question), Kolountzakis–Spyridakis (polytopal unions, a case already known by the authors’ account), Seck (planar convex Schiffer claim, unrefereed and with a brief proof step), Dai et al. (uniformly convex, large-eigenvalue, threshold unquantified), Puls (homogeneous spaces) and Cao-Labora–Fernández (sphere). The old claims of a full solution are Liu 2007 (both parts withdrawn by the author), Ramm 2013 (planar, ball-diffeomorphic hypothesis) and Ramm 2016 (R³); none has uptake I could find, and two of them conflict with the 2026 counterexamples if their hypotheses are met. AI involvement is established on the authors’ own account only for Guo: the Zenodo records say the work was ‘carried out with the assistance of AI models’ and the author’s README says the constructions, proofs, verification code and text were ‘produced with AI models’ and ‘audited with AI assistance’. That README sentence is the only authors’ account in my sources that describes load-bearing production, and it is repository-level. For Colbrook and Stepaniants the authors’ AI declaration says ChatGPT 5.5 in the form of codex ‘was used to help debug an early version of some of the code’; that is debugging, so per the protocol it is not placed in ai.systems and none_found is false. For Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont the names GPT-5.6 and Claude models appear only in Wikipedia and the tracker; I did not find the authors saying so in readable text, so no system is listed. Close calls: whether the topology in the statement is simply connected or connected complement (equivalent for bounded planar domains, but the higher-dimensional reading is not fixed); whether Colbrook’s planar result is a resolution or only a counterexample to one reading; and whether Guo’s v2 planar example meets Seck’s or Dai et al.’s hypotheses. Shape-of-result caveat: the Pompeiu property of Guo’s planar example is in Section 33 of v2, which I did not read.
competing_reading: A reader who discounts unrefereed, computer-assisted preprints by single or same-team authors would record the problem as open with a set of unconfirmed counterexamples, and would treat Ramm 2013 and 2016 as unrefuted claims. A reader who accepts validated certificates as checkable would say the planar conjecture as worded is false (Colbrook–Stepaniants and Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont agree in the plane) and that higher-dimensional convex cases are false too. On the AI question, a reader could say Guo’s ‘assistance’ wording in Zenodo is the authors’ account and the README is a generic statement, so the AI role is not load-bearing; the README sentence, however, says the constructions and proofs were produced with AI models, which is load-bearing on its face. On the topology, a reader who takes Ramm’s ball-diffeomorphism hypothesis as part of the statement would exclude Colbrook’s domain from the class only if its closure fails to be diffeomorphic to a ball, which it does not appear to.
what_would_settle_it: (1) An independent run of the Colbrook–Stepaniants certificate checker and of Guo’s Arb scripts, and a referee report on either. (2) The full Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont text, past the readable 100k characters, for an AI declaration, and the Lean repository checked for sorry and for who wrote the Lean proof. (3) The Ramm 2013 and 2016 full texts, to see whether the ball-diffeomorphism hypothesis and the ‘P-property implies ball’ direction are as quoted. (4) Seck’s Theorem 4.2 proof and whether Guo’s planar k = 1 domain satisfies its convexity and Dirichlet-eigenvalue hypotheses. (5) Dai et al.’s α₀(Ω) and whether Guo’s planar eigenvalue exceeds it. (6) Guo’s second paper (the infinitely-many-dimensions claim) located as a text, and its Section 33 Pompeiu proof for the planar example. (7) Journal submissions or acceptances for any 2026 preprint, checked on arXiv journal-reference fields.

event.what_happened: Matthew J. Colbrook and George Stepaniants, ‘A computer-assisted counterexample to the planar Pompeiu and Schiffer conjectures’, arXiv:2608.01579 (math.AP, cross-list math-ph and math.SP), v1 only. Theorem 1.1: a bounded, simply connected, noncircular domain Ω in R² with real-analytic Jordan boundary, invariant under the dihedral group D₁₀ of order 20, and a nonconstant real u with (Δ + k²)u = 0 in Ω, u = 1 and ∂νu = 0 on ∂Ω, for k in (31.967007261, 31.967007293). Lemma 1.2 (the Fourier transform of the indicator vanishes on the circle of radius k) gives failure of the Pompeiu property. Stated as a counterexample to Schiffer’s conjecture and to the planar Pompeiu conjecture for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains. A Shortcake talk by Stepaniants was given at Princeton on 16 Sep 2026; this is a talk, not a review.
event.delivers: Establishes (if correct) that one bounded simply connected noncircular real-analytic planar domain lacks the Pompeiu property. Planar and simply connected only: nothing for n ≥ 3, and no statement on other topologies. A single failing non-ball is enough to refute the planar form of the conjecture as worded.
event.remains: Every dimension n ≥ 3; the full description of which planar domains fail the property; the converse structure for other topologies.

checked_by.who: Frozen verifier, exact numerical centre, interval enclosures and certificate checker (Zenodo deposit MColbrook/Pompeiu_Schiffer v1.0.0, creator George Stepaniants)
checked_by.qualification: Authors’ own code; not an independent check
checked_by.what_they_did: Provides reproduction scripts and a certificate checker

machine_checked.system: Validated numerical certificate (radii-polynomial / Newton–Kantorovich contraction; MPFR interval arithmetic at ‘256256 bits’ as printed; not Lean)

event.directly_checkable: The domain is a conformal image φ(𝔻) with φ a ten-fold symmetric map close to an explicitly listed degree-301 polynomial. Certified constants as read: Y ≤ 1.59×10⁻¹⁰, Z ≤ 0.621, C₂ ≤ 122, C₃ ≤ 0.012, unique zero in a ball of radius 10⁻⁶. Hand-checking is infeasible; the deposit carries the checker. I did not re-run it.
event.doubts: No independent reproduction, expert review or journal acceptance found. The argument depends on the authors’ interval code. The fetched text includes an ‘AI declaration’ (see ai) about debugging. Dai et al. (2025) do not contradict this domain as far as the record shows, since its convexity is not stated.
event.direction: Against the conjecture as worded for n = 2 simply connected domains: asserts a non-ball member of the class lacks the Pompeiu property, where the conjecture says only balls do.
event.object: Ω = φ(𝔻): a bounded simply connected noncircular planar domain with real-analytic Jordan boundary, D₁₀-symmetric, close to an explicit degree-301 polynomial image of the disc. A nonconstant real eigenfunction u with ∂νu = 0 and u = 1 on the boundary exists for k near 31.967 (Schiffer counterexample). By Green’s identity the indicator’s Fourier transform vanishes on the circle of radius k, so Ω lacks the Pompeiu property. Existence is non-constructive, certified by a computer-assisted contraction around a numerical centre.

judgement.why: The statement's conjecture is the universal claim that a bounded simply connected (Lipschitz) domain failing the Pompeiu property must be a ball. One non-ball counterexample in the class refutes that claim outright, so I scored Colbrook–Stepaniants and Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont as whole and refuted, but unreviewed. Interval certificates and an authors' own Lean build are not digestion, and neither is checkable by hand. Guo v2 includes a planar convex example, so it is also scored whole. Guo events that cover only dimensions n ≥ 3 are scored case, following the record's split between the planar and higher-dimensional questions. Schiffer-only, Berenstein, spherical, discrete and homogeneous-space results are variants. Kolountzakis–Spyridakis re-proves a case known since Williams 1976, so it is none. For AI role, Guo's README says the constructions and proofs were 'produced with AI models', which is generated. Colbrook's AI use was debugging only, and the Cao-Labora AI attribution rests only on secondary sources, so both are none. I judged Ramm's 2013 and 2016 claims not_credible: they have had no uptake in over a decade, later work treats the problem as open, and they directly conflict with the 2026 counterexamples.
judgement.doubts: There are two close calls on scope. First, whether a higher-dimensional-only counterexample (Guo dim 4, dims 4/6, v1, second paper) should count as whole rather than case: if the conjecture is read as dimension-free, any one counterexample refutes it. Second, whether the statement's vague 'topology of domains' wording makes a planar counterexample only a case. For the Guo Zenodo-only events, the event-level quote says only 'assistance'; I rated them generated because the repository README that hosts this work says the proofs were AI-produced. The Pompeiu-failure proof for Guo's v2 planar example is in an unread section.
judgement.by: judging pass (JUDGE.md), claude-opus-5-5; not the researching agent and not a human reviewer
